_comment: Which pages each role may see. Read by src/users/services/role_service.py
and served to the browser at GET /api/users/role-pages, so the sidebar and
the client-side routes are driven by this one file.
HIDING A NAV ITEM IS NOT ACCESS CONTROL. This file decides what the UI
offers; the API enforces the same rules independently with require_admin,
and tests/test_users_api.py asserts a ROLE_USER is refused by the settings
endpoints even when it calls them directly.
Paths must match frontend/src/layout/navigation.js.
/swing and /btst are NOT gated by the strategy toggle. Each is the
decision journal of an automated strategy, and a journal is history:
switching the strategy off must not hide the record of what it did (root
CLAUDE.md section 3a).
A page listed here can still be hidden by a FEATURE toggle: the effective
set is these pages intersected with what the enabled strategies and
capabilities grant (see pages_for_role). Only /live, /chain, /notes and
/reports are gated that way; the rest, including everything that shows
history, are never withdrawn.
/live is the Crude Oil screen and is granted by the live-price
CAPABILITY, which only mcx-crude-options declares. It used to be granted
by ANY strategy being live, which left it in the sidebar showing a front
contract no running strategy had. /profile stays here and stays a real
route; it is simply not in the sidebar -- the header account menu is
where it lives now.
/ipo is the IPO dashboard and is granted to BOTH roles: any signed-in
user may read all three tabs. The three ACTIONS -- Applied, Accepted UPI
Mandate, Reject -- are admin-only and are refused by require_admin on the
action endpoints, whatever the buttons show. It is not a strategy and not
a capability, so it is not gated by any feature toggle; its own on/off
switch is the config property ipo.scheduler_enabled, which stops the
clock and the reminders without ever hiding the page or its history.
/connections owns anything this application authenticates to and calls
over the network -- the Dhan credentials, and the Telegram bot that
carries alerts out and commands in. Admin-only, like /settings and
/health, and NOT strategy-gated: it is how you fix the credentials the
strategies run on, so a toggle must never be able to hide it.

ROLE_ACCOUNT_ADMIN.label: Account admin
ROLE_ACCOUNT_ADMIN.description: Full access, including Settings, system health, portfolios, strategies and user management.

ROLE_USER.label: User
ROLE_USER.description: Everything except Settings, Connections, System Health and Strategies. Sees portfolios and the user list but cannot change either.
